channel.title: The Agentic Bible
channel.description: Articles on agentic coding that take a position and show the grounds under it.

item.title: An agent takes a given for an inevitability
item.description: An agent that finds an approach, a document or a rule in your codebase concludes that this is how things must be. The two obvious remedies — more context, and an instruction to be critical — both fail, and they fail with consequences that will keep humans useful for some time yet.

item.title: TEND: four lenses for the prose your agents write
item.description: Agents write a great deal of prose, and write more of it when they see that there is already a lot. Four lenses — tightness, existence, negation, durability — catch nearly all of what goes wrong.

item.title: Drive your agents from the web, not from the CLI
item.description: Most people stay in a local terminal because a terminal is where serious work happens and a browser tab is where it doesn’t. That is a feeling, not an argument, and the three things you get for giving it up are not small ones.
